subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Mud Brick: Humanity's First Building Material
description: One-minute skill: Mud Brick: Humanity's First Building Material.

hook.text: The oldest known building material is mud. Mixed with straw, it becomes surprisingly strong.

buildup.text: Adobe bricks are sun-dried mud blocks. They've been used for 10,000 years across every continent.

discovery.text: Straw fibers act like rebar in concrete — they hold the mud together when it cracks under stress.

twist.text: The city of Shibam in Yemen has mud-brick skyscrapers up to 11 stories tall. They've stood for 500 years.

climax.text: Today, one-third of the world's population still lives in earthen buildings. Mud never went away.

punchline.text: The first building material is still in service.

quiz.question: Why is straw added to mud bricks?
options: It makes the bricks lighter for easier transport
It holds the mud together when cracks form, like rebar
It insulates the bricks from heat and cold
